look_here_first: Go straight to the giant velvety leaves and mature fruit. Velvetleaf has a large ~15 × 20 mm schizocarp forming a conspicuous crown of mericarps with 3–6 mm divergent spines; the style is 13–15-branched.

project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO and Flora of North America treat the species as introduced/naturalized in Texas.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Learner comparison only; exclude from confirmed-native metrics.

best_field_traits: many mericarps with long divergent beaks
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Much larger-leaved and more strongly beaked than A. fruticosum; annual weed habit is also distinctive.
morphology_keys.flower: Calyx ~10 mm, lobes erect in fruit; pale-yellow petals 8–13 mm; staminal column glabrous; style 13–15-branched.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Schizocarp broadly ovoid, about 15 × 20 mm; mericarp apex spinose with divergent 3–6 mm spines; 3 seeds per mericarp, seeds 3–4 mm.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Much larger-leaved and more strongly beaked than A. fruticosum; annual weed habit is also distinctive.

fastest_traits: Very large soft cordate leaves 8–15 cm
Fruit ~15 × 20 mm; mericarp spines 3–6 mm and divergent

look_alikes.distinction: A. fruticosum is a woody-based subshrub with much smaller foliage, 6–9 style branches and a compact 8–9 mm fruit lacking long divergent spines.
A. incanum has only 5 style branches, a pubescent staminal column and a compact 7–9 mm cask-shaped fruit.
